name: Mohamed Al-Fayed
milestone_by_age_26: No material independent business milestone by age 26; was an employee in Khashoggi's furniture import business and married into the Khashoggi family at 25, but his independent wealth (shipping company, advising Sultan of Brunei, Ritz, Harrods) came in his 30s-40s.
early_history_summary: Born to a primary school teacher in Alexandria, Al-Fayed sold Coca-Cola and sewing machines as a young man before being hired in 1952 by Adnan Khashoggi's furniture import business. He married Samira Khashoggi in 1954 but had not yet built an independent business empire by 26.
family_context_summary: Born to an Egyptian primary school teacher; mother died when he was four. Raised by stepmother in a poor district of Alexandria.
evidence_summary: Al-Fayed's early business life was tied to the Khashoggi family through employment and marriage, not independent achievement. His major acquisitions (Ritz Paris 1979, Harrods 1985) and advisory roles (Sultan of Brunei 1966) all came well after age 26. No material, independently verifiable milestone by 26 was found.

name: Tomas Tranströmer
milestone_by_age_26: Published debut poetry collection '17 dikter' (17 Poems) in 1954 at age 23, acclaimed as one of the most significant literary debuts of the decade and establishing him as the leading Swedish poet of his generation.
early_history_summary: Tranströmer began writing poetry as a teenager at Södra Latin Gymnasium in Stockholm, publishing in student magazines in the late 1940s. His debut collection '17 dikter' was published by Bonniers in 1954 when he was 23, immediately establishing his reputation for original metaphors, musicality, and formal precision. He continued studying psychology at Stockholm University while writing.
family_context_summary: Raised by his mother Helmy, a schoolteacher, following her divorce from his father Gösta, an editor. Middle-class Swedish upbringing in Stockholm.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an editor and mother was a schoolteacher, providing a cultured literary-educational environment, though no direct evidence of parental literary mentorship is documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early writing, literary debut, Swedish literary culture, gymnasium education
evidence_summary: Tranströmer began publishing poems in student magazines as a teenager and had his debut collection '17 dikter' published at 23 by Bonniers, one of Sweden's premier publishers. The collection was immediately recognized as a major literary debut. His mother was a schoolteacher and his father an editor, providing a cultured environment. He studied at Södra Latin Gymnasium, a selective Stockholm school, before attending Stockholm University. His distinctive poetic voice was already fully formed at debut.

name: Tony Curtis
milestone_by_age_26: Landed his first starring role in 'The Prince Who Was a Thief' (released June 1951) at age 26, a box office hit that established him as a leading man at Universal Pictures.
early_history_summary: Born Bernard Schwartz in the Bronx, Curtis served in the Navy during WWII, then studied acting at the New School in New York. He was discovered by casting agent Joyce Selznick, signed with Universal Pictures in 1948, and worked his way up through bit parts and supporting roles in 1949-1950 before receiving his first starring role in 1951.
family_context_summary: Born to Hungarian-Jewish immigrant parents in the Bronx; his mother was schizophrenic and frequently institutionalized. Grew up in poverty in a tough neighborhood. Served in the Navy during WWII.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were working-class immigrants with no connection to entertainment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hollywood studio system, GI Bill, Universal contract, Selznick discovery, postwar film boom
evidence_summary: Curtis leveraged the GI Bill to study acting in New York, was discovered by Joyce Selznick (niece of legendary producer David O. Selznick), and signed with Universal Pictures in 1948. He rose through bit parts to his first starring role in 1951 at age 26, benefiting from the postwar Hollywood studio system. His good looks and the studio's promotional machinery (including a 'Win a Weekend with Tony Curtis' contest) accelerated his rise. His working-class immigrant background and Navy service preceded his acting career.

name: Jean-Paul Belmondo
milestone_by_age_26: Breakthrough role in Godard's 'Breathless' (À bout de souffle) was filmed in mid-1959 and released in May 1960 when Belmondo was 27; no material milestone by age 26 found. Earlier film roles (1958-1959) were minor or supporting parts.
early_history_summary: Son of sculptor Paul Belmondo, Jean-Paul studied at the Conservatoire National Supérieur d'Art Dramatique and performed in provincial theatre. His early film roles from 1956-1959 were minor, including cut scenes and supporting parts, before his breakthrough in Breathless at age 27.
family_context_summary: Son of renowned French sculptor Paul Belmondo who taught at the Académie des Beaux-Arts; grew up in Neuilly-sur-Seine, an affluent Paris suburb, and on the Left Bank.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a prominent sculptor and academic, providing cultural capital and artistic environment, though not directly in film.
evidence_summary: Belmondo's breakthrough came with Breathless (1960) at age 27, not by 26. His pre-26 filmography included minor roles in Sois belle et tais-toi (1958), Young Sinners (1958), and a supporting role in Chabrol's À double tour (1959), but none constituted a material milestone. He trained at the Conservatoire and had provincial theatre experience, but stardom arrived after 26.

name: Mohamed Salah
milestone_by_age_26: At age 25, scored 32 Premier League goals in the 2017-18 season (a record for a 38-game season), won PFA Player of the Year, and led Liverpool to the Champions League final.
early_history_summary: Salah joined Al-Mokawloon's youth academy at 14, commuting hours daily from his village, and made his senior debut at 18. He signed for Basel in 2012 at 20, won two Swiss Super League titles, then moved to Chelsea in 2014. After limited opportunities at Chelsea, loans to Fiorentina and Roma revitalized his career, leading to a permanent move to Roma and then Liverpool in 2017, where he had his record-breaking season at 25.
family_context_summary: Born to middle-class parents in Nagrig, a village north of Cairo. His father was a merchant. Salah's family supported his football ambitions, allowing him to leave school early for daily training commutes to Cairo.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connection to professional football.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Al-Mokawloon academy, Basel pipeline, physical speed, daily training commute, Egyptian youth national teams
evidence_summary: Salah's exceptional speed and talent were noticed early; he joined Al-Mokawloon at 14 and made his senior debut at 18. His performances at the 2011 U-20 World Cup and for Egypt's national team attracted Basel, who scouted him specifically. After Chelsea, his development at Roma and then Liverpool culminated in a record-breaking 2017-18 season at age 25 with 32 Premier League goals and PFA Player of the Year. His early commute from village to Cairo for training showed exceptional dedication from a young age.

name: Alain Resnais
milestone_by_age_26: Made 'Van Gogh' (1948), his first 35mm film, at age 26, which won international awards including recognition at the Venice Film Festival and established his international reputation as a filmmaker.
early_history_summary: Born in Vannes, Brittany to a pharmacist, Resnais was given a cine-camera at 12 and made amateur 8mm films as a teenager. He moved to Paris in 1939 to study acting, then enrolled at IDHEC film school in 1943. After military service, he returned to Paris in 1946 and began making short films about artists, leading to the breakthrough 'Van Gogh' in 1948.
family_context_summary: Son of a pharmacist in Vannes, Brittany; enjoyed a comfortable, cultured upbringing with parents who shared a keen interest in classic literature, photography, painting, and comic books.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IDHEC film school, Kodak cine-camera at 12, Paris cultural milieu, Jean Grémillon mentorship, Pierre Braunberger producer
evidence_summary: Resnais was given a Kodak cine-camera at 12 and made amateur films throughout his teens. He studied at IDHEC (France's premier film school) from 1943-45, where Jean Grémillon was a key influence. His comfortable cultured family background supported early artistic exploration. In Paris, he befriended actor Gérard Philipe and made early 16mm films. Producer Pierre Braunberger financed his 35mm breakthrough 'Van Gogh' (1948), which won international awards. His proximity to the Parisian art and film world was a major accelerator.

name: Gigliola Cinquetti
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Sanremo Music Festival and the Eurovision Song Contest in 1964 at age 16 with 'Non ho l'età,' becoming Italy's first Eurovision winner and the youngest winner in the contest's history at that time.
early_history_summary: Born in Verona, Cinquetti began her career at 15 by winning the Castrocaro Music Festival, which led to her Sanremo participation. Her debut single was released in late 1963, and in early 1964 she won Sanremo and then Eurovision at 16, launching a major international recording career.
family_context_summary: Born in Verona, Italy; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond her place of birth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sanremo Festival, Eurovision, Castrocaro Festival, Italian music industry, teenage breakthrough
evidence_summary: Cinquetti won the Castrocaro Music Festival at 15, which served as a pipeline to the Sanremo Festival, Italy's most prestigious music competition. Winning Sanremo at 16 earned her the right to represent Italy at Eurovision, which she also won, making her an international star. The festival system provided a powerful distribution and discovery platform. Her song 'Non ho l'età' became a major European hit. Family background is not well documented in reviewed sources.

name: Andrew Wiles
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored with John Coates the paper 'On the Conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer' (Inventiones Mathematicae, 1977) at age 24, making the first progress on one of mathematics' fundamental conjectures, and became Assistant Professor at Harvard University the same year.
early_history_summary: Wiles discovered Fermat's Last Theorem at age 10 in a library book and was captivated. He studied mathematics at Merton College, Oxford, graduating in 1974, then began graduate work at Clare College, Cambridge under John Coates. His early research on elliptic curves led to the Coates-Wiles result on the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture in 1977, published when he was 24, and he joined Harvard as Assistant Professor the same year.
family_context_summary: Born in Cambridge to theologian Maurice Frank Wiles (who became Dean of Clare College) and Patricia Wiles. Father was appointed lecturer at University of Ibadan, Nigeria when Andrew was 2, returning to Cambridge in 1959. Grew up in an academic household.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a theologian and academic at Cambridge, providing an intellectual environment, though not in mathematics specifically.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cambridge academic family, Merton College Oxford, Clare College Cambridge, John Coates mentorship, Harvard appointment, early fascination with Fermat
evidence_summary: Wiles grew up in an academic Cambridge family and discovered Fermat's Last Theorem at 10, committing to solve it. He studied at Oxford and then Cambridge under John Coates, who provided sustained mentorship. The Coates-Wiles paper (1977) made the first progress on the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, a landmark result published when Wiles was 24. He simultaneously became Assistant Professor at Harvard. His extraordinary concentration and deep technical skill in number theory were evident from his early career. The Cambridge-Oxford-Harvard pipeline was central to his development.

name: Miguel Muñoz
milestone_by_age_26: Helped Celta Vigo finish fourth in La Liga and reach the 1948 Copa del Generalísimo final, scoring in the final, at age 26, before signing for Real Madrid the following season.
early_history_summary: Born in Madrid, Muñoz played for various junior teams before joining Logroñés (1943), Racing Santander (1944-46), and Celta Vigo (1946-48). His strong 1947-48 season at Celta, including reaching the cup final, earned him a transfer to Real Madrid in 1948, where he became captain and won three European Cups as a player.
family_context_summary: Born in Madrid; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond his place of birth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Madrid football culture, La Liga career, Celta Vigo cup run, Pahíño partnership, Real Madrid signing
evidence_summary: Muñoz played for junior teams in Madrid before progressing through Logroñés, Racing Santander, and Celta Vigo in the Spanish football pyramid. His partnership with Pahíño at Celta in 1947-48 was productive, leading to a fourth-place La Liga finish and a Copa del Generalísimo final appearance where he scored. This earned him a move to Real Madrid at 26, where he became captain and won three European Cups. Family background is not documented. His career was built through steady progression in Spanish football's post-war era.

name: Richard Attenborough
milestone_by_age_26: By age 19 was an in-demand West End actor and public figure; gave acclaimed stage performance as Pinkie in 'Brighton Rock' and made first credited film role in 'The Hundred Pound Window' (1944), establishing a sustained acting career by his early 20s.
early_history_summary: Attenborough began acting at Leicester's Little Theatre before winning a scholarship to RADA at 17. While still a student, he made his West End debut and first film appearance in 'In Which We Serve' (1942). His stage performance as Pinkie in 'Brighton Rock' drew critical acclaim, and he was conscripted into the RAF Film Unit before continuing his film career post-war.
family_context_summary: Born in Cambridge to Frederick Attenborough, principal of University College, Leicester, and Mary Attenborough. Grew up in an academic household; younger brother is naturalist David Attenborough. Family was supportive of the arts.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a university college principal, providing a cultured, educated environment. No direct family connection to film or theatre, but the family's social position facilitated access to education and cultural opportunities.
primary_early_advantage_tags: RADA scholarship, Leicester Little Theatre, West End debut, Noël Coward mentorship, RAF Film Unit, academic family
evidence_summary: Attenborough's rise was accelerated by RADA training, early West End opportunities, and connections to influential figures like Noël Coward and agent Al Parker. His academic family background (father was a college principal) provided cultural capital. The wartime British film industry offered roles for young actors, and his Brighton Rock stage performance drew critical acclaim. The RAF Film Unit experience further deepened his film knowledge. By his early 20s, he was an established actor with multiple film credits and a public profile.

name: César Luis Menotti
milestone_by_age_26: As a player by age 26, Menotti was at Racing Club (1964) with Argentina national caps, but no standout individual milestone; his fame and material success came as manager of the 1978 World Cup-winning Argentina team.
early_history_summary: Born in Rosario, Menotti played for local club Unión Americana before debuting for Rosario Central in 1960 at age 21. He played for Rosario Central (1960-63), Racing Club (1964), and Boca Juniors (1965-66), with national team caps from 1963, but was a journeyman player whose legacy was built as a manager.
family_context_summary: Born in Rosario to Antonio Menotti, a former Rosario Central player in the amateur era who died of cancer when César was 16. Mother was Olga Fasola. Father was a fan of Rosario Central, which influenced César's club allegiance.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father played one official match for Rosario Central in the amateur era and was a passionate club fan, providing a football-cultural environment, though not professional-level advantage.
evidence_summary: Menotti's playing career was modest: he debuted for Rosario Central at 21, played for Racing at 26, and earned Argentina caps, but no material individual milestone distinguished him by 26. His father's death when he was 16 created financial pressure that pushed him toward professional football. His legendary status came entirely from managing Argentina to the 1978 World Cup, not from his playing career. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Peter Brook
milestone_by_age_26: By age 22 was Director of Productions at the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden (1947-1950), having already directed at Stratford-upon-Avon at 21 and Birmingham Repertory Theatre at 20, described by Barry Jackson as 'the youngest earthquake I've known.'
early_history_summary: Brook staged his first production (Marlowe's Dr Faustus) at the Torch Theatre in London in 1943 at age 18 while still an undergraduate at Oxford. He was hired by Barry Jackson at Birmingham Rep in 1945 at 20, directed Love's Labour's Lost at Stratford-upon-Avon in 1946 at 21, and became Director of Productions at the Royal Opera House in 1947 at 22, making him one of the most precocious directors in British theatre history.
family_context_summary: Born in Chiswick to a middle-class family; attended Westminster and Gresham's schools before going up to Oxford in 1942. His brother became a psychiatrist. Family background details are sparse in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources in detail; family was sufficiently affluent to send him to Westminster School and Gresham's, suggesting comfortable middle-class or upper-middle-class background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Barry Jackson mentorship, Birmingham Rep, Stratford-upon-Avon, Royal Opera House, Oxford education, Hugh Beaumont network, early precocity
evidence_summary: Brook was a prodigy who directed his first play at 18 while at Oxford. Barry Jackson at Birmingham Rep hired him at 20 and became a key mentor, inviting him to Stratford and giving him professional opportunities far beyond his years. By 22, Brook was Director of Productions at the Royal Opera House, one of the most prestigious positions in British theatre. His network included influential figures like Hugh Beaumont of HM Tennent management and Jackson, who called him 'the youngest earthquake.' His education at Westminster, Gresham's, and Oxford provided the cultural and social platform for this precocious rise.
